questions.prompt: A tool call includes tenant_id='northstar'. What establishes the tenant?
questions.explanation: Tool arguments and prompts are untrusted input. Tenant scope comes from authenticated state and policy.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility belongs in a provider adapter?
questions.explanation: Adapters contain provider mechanics; application policy stays provider-independent.

questions.prompt: A mock generator passes all unit tests. What remains unproven?
questions.explanation: Deterministic mocks prove application behavior, not a live model's behavior.

questions.prompt: Which retrieval order is safest?
questions.explanation: Scope filtering must precede ranking and downstream exposure.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of async in this course?
options: Efficient waiting on I/O with cancellation/deadlines
questions.explanation: Async primarily helps I/O-bound concurrency; it requires explicit budget and cancellation discipline.

questions.prompt: Which dependency belongs in a development group rather than runtime dependencies?
options: A library imported by the service
The HTTP client used at runtime
The validation library used for requests
questions.explanation: Test tooling should not become a production runtime requirement.

questions.prompt: Why report forbidden outcomes separately from blocked attempts?
options: They have different denominators and operational meaning
questions.explanation: An attempted attack, a prevented violation, an actual violation, and valid work blocked are distinct populations.

questions.prompt: What must happen after structured generation?
options: Validate business, authorization, and evidence invariants
Ask the same model to approve itself
questions.explanation: Schema validity is only one boundary; semantic and policy validation use trusted state.

questions.prompt: The model call times out after the request deadline. What is the correct default?
options: Return a fabricated fallback as success
Continue in the background without ownership
Stop work and return/record a timeout failure
questions.explanation: Cancellation and explicit terminal state protect the user SLA and resource budget.

questions.prompt: When should a direct one-function design be preferred?
options: For a disposable bounded exploration where added boundaries do not earn their cost
questions.explanation: Architecture should be proportional; abstractions have carrying cost.

questions.prompt: Which item should normally be excluded from telemetry?
questions.explanation: Record observable decisions and identifiers, not private reasoning.

questions.prompt: What is the best definition of state of the art for a production decision?
options: The tool with the most stars
The best evidenced fit for actual constraints
questions.explanation: Maturity, fit, safety, operations, cost, portability, and evidence matter more than novelty.

questions.prompt: Which value should represent one intended business effect across client and worker retries?
questions.explanation: A stable logical operation ID lets durable state associate repeated delivery attempts with one intended effect.

questions.prompt: A write timed out after it may have committed. What should a retrying worker do first?
questions.explanation: The outcome is unknown, so authoritative state must be checked before another side effect can be attempted safely.

questions.prompt: Why does an SQS visibility timeout not prove exactly-once application behavior?
options: Duplicate delivery and external side effects remain possible
questions.explanation: Visibility temporarily hides a received message, but redelivery and effects outside the broker still require application safeguards.

questions.prompt: What is the safest default when version 1 arrives after version 2 was committed?
options: Reject or record version 1 as stale
questions.explanation: A domain-version condition preserves the newer projection despite transport reordering or delayed retry.

questions.prompt: Three layers each retry a call up to three times. What risk should the design review expose?
options: Up to 27 attempts for one operation
questions.explanation: Nested retry policies multiply work and can overload a degraded dependency, so retry ownership and budgets must be explicit.

questions.prompt: Which signal is more useful than queue depth alone for an asynchronous completion SLO?
options: Number of AWS regions in a slide
questions.explanation: Oldest-message age reveals how long accepted work waits and directly connects backlog to a user-visible completion objective.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes a production-ready dead-letter process?
options: Alert, inspect, repair, and redrive at a controlled rate
questions.explanation: Dead-letter quarantine needs ownership, safe diagnostic context, a repair decision, and idempotent rate-limited redrive.

questions.prompt: When does a work queue fit better than a pub/sub topic?
options: Every subscriber must receive the event
One consumer group should own each independent job
questions.explanation: A queue distributes independently owned work, while pub/sub is intended to deliver a notification to multiple subscribers.

questions.prompt: What does a conditional version write prevent?
options: A stale or conflicting update silently replacing current state
questions.explanation: Compare-and-set or optimistic version checks make stale and concurrent conflicts observable instead of accepting last writer wins.

questions.prompt: What does delivery attempts divided by successful logical operations measure?
questions.explanation: Work amplification exposes retry and duplicate overhead per successful business outcome and helps detect retry storms.

questions.prompt: What does a 202 Accepted response from an asynchronous API establish?
options: The system accepted ownership under its documented durability contract
questions.explanation: Acceptance and business completion are separate states; the client must observe the operation resource for a terminal outcome.

questions.prompt: An event contains tenant_id='northstar'. What authorizes the worker to access Northstar data?
options: Trusted workload identity plus application policy
questions.explanation: Event data is untrusted input; workload identity and trusted policy establish whether the worker may perform the requested action.

questions.prompt: A JWT parses and contains role='admin'. What has parsing established?
questions.explanation: Claims remain untrusted until issuer, key, signature, algorithm, token use, audience, and time are validated.

questions.prompt: What is the safer stable key for a federated user identity?
questions.explanation: OpenID Connect subjects are scoped to an issuer, so the pair prevents collisions across identity providers.

questions.prompt: Why should an API reject an ID token presented as its authorization credential?
options: It is intended for the client rather than the resource server
questions.explanation: The API needs an access token issued for its resource audience and use, not a client authentication assertion.

questions.prompt: What does valid workload authentication prove by itself?
options: Every customer record it may access
questions.explanation: Authentication identifies the process; application policy still decides tenant, subject, resource, action, and obligations.

questions.prompt: Which child delegation is valid?
options: Fewer actions and resources with no later expiry
A different tenant with the same role
questions.explanation: A child capability must attenuate every bounded dimension and can never widen authority inherited from its parent.

questions.prompt: What is the policy enforcement point responsible for?
options: Protecting the real action and enforcing decisions and obligations
questions.explanation: The enforcement point intercepts the operation, obtains a decision, satisfies obligations, and records the actual outcome.

questions.prompt: Why must a broadly privileged service also check delegated user authority?
options: Technical reach does not authorize using it for every caller
questions.explanation: Intersecting actor and subject authority prevents a caller from coercing the service into becoming a confused deputy.

questions.prompt: Which change must invalidate an approval receipt for a proposed exception?
questions.explanation: Changing a consequential parameter changes the canonical proposal digest and requires a new independent review.

questions.prompt: How should an exact retry behave after approval and execution commit atomically?
options: Return the recorded result without authorizing new work
questions.explanation: Stable operation identity permits safe reconciliation while the consumed approval remains unavailable to other work.

questions.prompt: Which model best represents nested sharing such as organization members viewing documents?
questions.explanation: Relationship-based systems model subject-relation-object tuples and derive access through a defined relationship graph.

questions.prompt: A user's entitlements change after a delegation was issued. What should the gateway do?
options: Detect staleness or re-evaluate current authority
questions.explanation: Authorization is lifecycle-sensitive, so current policy data or versions must invalidate stale delegated authority.

questions.prompt: Why report forbidden outcomes separately from valid work blocked?
options: They measure different safety and usability populations
False denial is a security success
questions.explanation: Unauthorized effects and false denials are different failures with different denominators, owners, and consequences.

questions.prompt: Which metadata must follow a source into every retrievable chunk?
options: Tenant, ACL, source/version/locator, digest, lifecycle, and processing versions
questions.explanation: Chunk-level policy and provenance make authorization, currency, deletion, reproduction, and citation verification enforceable.

questions.prompt: Why authorize and lifecycle-filter chunks before retrieval and reranking?
options: To keep unauthorized or stale evidence out of scoring and downstream context
questions.explanation: Late filtering can leak IDs, scores, timing, or text, waste candidate budget, and expose forbidden content to later components.

questions.prompt: Which query most strongly justifies retaining a lexical BM25-style branch?
options: An exact identifier such as UW-17
questions.explanation: Sparse retrieval is strong for exact identifiers, rare names, codes, numbers, and terms that dense representations may blur.

questions.prompt: What does reciprocal rank fusion avoid assuming?
options: That raw sparse and dense scores use a shared calibrated scale
questions.explanation: RRF combines positions rather than incomparable score magnitudes, making it a practical hybrid baseline before calibrated fusion.

questions.prompt: A new source version is flagged as poisoned. What is the safest default?
options: Publish it because it is newest
Quarantine it without silently replacing the known-good version
questions.explanation: Recency is not authority or safety; quarantine prevents promotion while an explicit review and recovery workflow proceeds.

questions.prompt: What should happen if an ingestion operation ID is retried with changed content?
options: Reject it as an operation conflict
questions.explanation: One stable operation ID represents one exact intent and cannot safely produce a different knowledge state on retry.

questions.prompt: A citation ID exists in the corpus but was not retrieved for this request. What should happen?
options: Reject it as a forged citation
questions.explanation: Corpus existence does not prove request-scoped retrieval, authorization, currency, or support for the generated claim.

questions.prompt: Why revalidate cited evidence after generation?
options: To close deletion, supersession, and permission-change races
questions.explanation: Retrieval is only a time-of-check; publication must confirm evidence is still unchanged, current, and authorized.

questions.prompt: What is the denominator of Recall@k?
options: All labelled relevant evidence in the evaluated population
questions.explanation: Recall@k measures how much of the labelled relevant set appears in the top-k; incomplete judgments can bias the result.

questions.prompt: Why can metadata filtering reduce approximate-nearest-neighbour recall?
options: Visited neighbours may consume the search budget before being filtered out
questions.explanation: Filter selectivity can exhaust bounded ANN exploration, motivating iterative scans, filter-aware indexes, partitioning, or exact fallback.

questions.prompt: When is GraphRAG justified over an established hybrid baseline?
options: When measured global or relational questions justify its extraction and operating cost
questions.explanation: Graph-derived knowledge adds extraction quality, lineage, deletion, latency, cost, and operational responsibilities that need measured value.

questions.prompt: What security property does an embedding provide by itself?
options: Neither; it remains sensitive derived data
questions.explanation: Embeddings can expose source information and must inherit access, encryption, retention, query, and deletion controls.

questions.prompt: A workflow and bounded agent have equal compliant success, but the agent costs more. What is the default choice?
options: The workflow unless variable-path evidence justifies agency
questions.explanation: The least-autonomous architecture wins when it meets the requirement with equal outcomes and lower control and operating cost.

questions.prompt: What does a valid tool schema establish?
questions.explanation: Structural validation is necessary, but trusted identity, workload capability, policy, and authoritative state decide permission.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility does MCP not remove?
options: Per-call authentication, authorization, and effect validation
questions.explanation: MCP standardizes communication surfaces; applications still govern who may invoke a tool and whether the result is safe and valid.

questions.prompt: A retrieved document asks the agent to export customer data. Which control prevents capability widening?
options: A fixed workload tool manifest and gateway policy
questions.explanation: Retrieved content is untrusted data; deterministic capability and authorization checks must reject a tool outside the run manifest.

questions.prompt: What should happen when an approved proposal's arguments change?
options: Issue a new approval bound to the changed digest
Ignore the change if the tool name is the same
questions.explanation: Approval applies to an exact action, target, argument digest, policy version, and validity window; changed content invalidates it.

questions.prompt: Why retain one logical operation ID across an uncertain retry?
options: To reconcile the intended effect and prevent duplication
questions.explanation: A stable operation identity and request digest let the executor distinguish replay from a different business intent.

questions.prompt: What prevents two resumed workers from silently overwriting run state?
options: Optimistic revision or an atomic transition
questions.explanation: A compare-and-set revision makes concurrent and stale checkpoint writes observable instead of accepting last-writer-wins.

questions.prompt: When should a cost or deadline limit be checked for a consequential tool?
options: At the end of the day
Only when the model requests it
questions.explanation: Post-effect accounting cannot prevent an irreversible over-budget action; reserve the relevant budget before execution.

questions.prompt: Who owns the trustworthy terminal state of an agent run?
options: The application using explicit completion invariants
questions.explanation: Completion depends on trusted evidence, validation, approval, effects, and budgets; model text cannot declare those facts.

questions.prompt: What is the denominator for cost per successful compliant task?
options: Successful tasks that also satisfied every required control
questions.explanation: Dividing total cost by compliant successes connects spend to the useful governed outcome rather than cheap failed requests.

questions.prompt: What does coordination tax include?
options: Extra calls, handoffs, duplicated work, merging, failures, and operations
questions.explanation: Multi-agent designs add total work, capability surfaces, shared-state and handoff failures, and operational ownership beyond latency.

questions.prompt: What does AgentCore Runtime hosting prove by itself?
options: Neither; application controls and evaluation remain necessary
Every tool effect is exactly once
questions.explanation: Managed hosting supplies runtime capabilities, not proof of business policy, idempotency, completion, quality, or safe tool behavior.
